rules.title: LDAP signing is not required on domain controllers
rules.description: Whether domain controllers require LDAP signing is a policy/registry setting that cannot be read through LDAP. The rule is reported as Not Evaluated.
rules.condition: Domain controller LDAP server signing requirement is not 'Require signing'.
rules.risk: Without required signing, LDAP traffic can be tampered with or relayed.
rules.recommendation: Check the 'Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements' policy on the domain controllers and plan enforcement following the Microsoft guidance.

rules.title: LDAP channel binding is not enforced on domain controllers
rules.description: LDAP channel binding is a registry/policy setting of the domain controllers that cannot be read through LDAP. The rule is reported as Not Evaluated.
rules.condition: Domain controller LDAP channel binding token policy is not 'Always'.
rules.risk: Without channel binding, LDAP over TLS authentication can be relayed.
rules.recommendation: Review the LDAP channel binding token requirements on the domain controllers and plan enforcement following the Microsoft guidance.

rules.title: Anonymous LDAP operations are allowed (dSHeuristics)
rules.description: The seventh character of the dSHeuristics attribute of the Directory Service object is '2', which allows anonymous LDAP operations.
rules.risk: Anonymous operations allow unauthenticated clients to read directory data, which helps attackers enumerate the environment.
rules.recommendation: Reset the seventh dSHeuristics character to 0 (or remove the setting) after confirming that no application depends on anonymous access.

rules.title: SMB signing is not required on domain controllers
rules.description: SMB signing configuration is a local server/policy setting that cannot be read through LDAP. The rule is reported as Not Evaluated.
rules.condition: Domain controller SMB server signing is not required.
rules.risk: Without required signing, SMB sessions can be tampered with or relayed.
rules.recommendation: Verify the Microsoft network server signing policy on the domain controllers following the Microsoft guidance.

rules.title: SMBv1 is enabled on domain controllers
rules.description: The SMBv1 state is a local server setting that cannot be read through LDAP. The rule is reported as Not Evaluated.
rules.risk: SMBv1 is a legacy protocol that should not be used.
rules.recommendation: Verify and remove SMBv1 from the domain controllers following the Microsoft guidance.

rules.title: NTLM authentication is not restricted
rules.description: LAN Manager authentication level and NTLM restrictions are policy/registry settings that cannot be read through LDAP. The rule is reported as Not Evaluated.
rules.condition: Network security: LAN Manager authentication level is lower than 'Send NTLMv2 response only'.
rules.risk: Legacy NTLM variants are weak and NTLM can be relayed.
rules.recommendation: Review the LAN Manager authentication level and NTLM auditing/restrictions following the Microsoft guidance.

rules.title: Group Policy Preferences file contains a cpassword
rules.description: Group Policy Preferences XML files in SYSVOL contain a cpassword attribute. The value is encrypted with a published key and can be decrypted by any domain user. The tool records only the file and setting; the value is never read into the report.
rules.condition: A GPP XML file in SYSVOL contains a non-empty cpassword attribute.
rules.risk: Any authenticated user can read SYSVOL and decrypt the credential, which may belong to a privileged or shared local account.
rules.recommendation: Remove the password from the Group Policy Preference, change the exposed credential and use an alternative such as Windows LAPS for local administrator passwords.

rules.title: External or forest trust without SID filtering
rules.description: SID filtering is reported as disabled for an external or forest trust (System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory GetSidFilteringStatus).
rules.condition: Trust classified as External or Forest where SID filtering status is disabled.
rules.risk: Without SID filtering, a compromised trusted domain can inject privileged SIDs into tickets (SID history) and escalate privileges in the trusting domain.
rules.recommendation: Review the need for the trust and enable SID filtering according to the Microsoft guidance (netdom trust /quarantine) after validating the impact on migrations that depend on SID history.

rules.title: Seamless SSO computer account password not rotated
rules.description: The AZUREADSSOACC computer account is used by Microsoft Entra Seamless SSO. Its Kerberos decryption key should be rolled over regularly, at least every {SeamlessSsoKeyRollDays} days according to Microsoft.
rules.risk: A long-lived Seamless SSO decryption key increases the impact of its theft; a stolen key allows forging Kerberos tickets that Entra ID accepts.
rules.recommendation: Roll over the Seamless SSO Kerberos decryption key following the Microsoft procedure and schedule the rollover.

applicableWhen.reason: No AZUREADSSOACC (Seamless SSO) account found: no evidence of this hybrid identity feature.

rules.title: Seamless SSO computer account has delegation configured
rules.description: The AZUREADSSOACC computer account has unconstrained delegation, constrained delegation with protocol transition, or resource-based constrained delegation (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity) configured.
rules.condition: AZUREADSSOACC with TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION, TRUSTED_TO_AUTH_FOR_DELEGATION or msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity set.
rules.risk: Delegation on this account may allow impersonation of users to the Entra Seamless SSO service or take-over of the account.
rules.recommendation: Remove the delegation from the AZUREADSSOACC account, following the Microsoft Defender for Identity and Seamless SSO guidance.

applicableWhen.reason: No AZUREADSSOACC (Seamless SSO) account found: no evidence of this hybrid identity feature.
